text:
ops-bot: PAGER: RIDGEWAY (prod-vpc) - auth failures affecting inference endpoints - HIGH priority
marisol oncall: I'm on it. Seeing lots of 401s from Ridgeway's VPC-hosted private deployment. Pager shows OIDC token refresh errors and mTLS handshake failures. @leo infra on call?
leo infra: here. can you paste an example error? logs?
marisol oncall: from ingress-proxy on the private control plane:
``
2025-07-07T18:12:03Z ingress[2972]: auth: token refresh failed: invalid_jwt_signature kid="k-20250707-rot1" subj="svc-agent@ridgeway"
2025-07-07T18:12:05Z xfer[1234]: mTLS handshake failed: certificate verify failed: CN mismatch, verify error depth=0
```
marisol oncall: timeline - started ~18:10 UTC, ramped to 100% erroneous for all Ridgeway tenants in that VPC. Dedicated pool requests get dropped with 502s and handshake errors.
ridgeway-sre: Confirming - our customers are getting 401s in our prod region. We're in a meet now, urgent pls.
leo infra: initial hypothesis: Ridgeway rotated their OIDC keys last night and their JWKS is serving a new key but control plane still expects old kid OR our JWKS cache eviction bug didn't pick up new key. Also seeing a client cert chain difference; looks like a cert swap happened around 18:05.
adele eng: jumping in - relevant components: private-control-plane auth service (verifies OIDC), gateway (mTLS client verification), and dedicated-pool ingress handling. Could be two simultaneous things: JWKS key rotation + Ridgeway pushed new client certs but didn't upload intermediate CA.
kevin sec: tagging sec. Need to know if this is just Ridgeway or all private customers. Any sign of global CA issues?
marisol oncall: only Ridgeway's VPC and their dedicated pool. Other customers unaffected.
ops-bot: DEPLOY-BOT: certificate rotation job completed for customer ridgeway at 2025-07-07T18:04:58Z
marisol oncall: OK that lines up. They rotated certs and keys. Our control plane is refusing tokens (invalid signature) and our pool rejecting mTLS.
leo infra: quick checks I ran:
- `curl -s https://oidc.ridgeway.example/.well-known/jwks.json | jq '.keys[].kid'` -> returns ["k-20250707-rot1"]
- our cached JWKS for ridgeway: kid `k-20250707-old1`
- gateway tls test:
  `openssl s_client -connect pool-ridgeway:443 -showcerts` -> shows leaf signed by intermediate `Ridgeway-Int-2025` but our truststore has `Ridgeway-Int-2024` only

leo infra: so tokens signed by the new kid fail to verify; mTLS fails because intermediate CA changed name.
marisol oncall: mitigation plan? we need to restore customer traffic quickly. options:
1) force JWKS refresh in control plane and reload truststore with new intermediate (fast but needs careful reload across private control plane).
2) if we can't trust new keys yet, add a short-lived bypass to accept previous sessions by skipping signature check for existing tokens (riskier), or redirect Ridgeway traffic to Hosted fallback where their OIDC metadata is accepted.
adele eng: we should avoid bypassing signature checks. Preferred: trigger JWKS refresh + hot-reload truststore. I can push a manual refresh endpoint call. @leo can you validate the new JWKS uses standard RS256 keys and produces valid signatures?
leo infra: validating now with example token from Ridgeway (redacted):
`jwt decode --in token.jwt --keyset https://oidc.ridgeway.example/.well-known/jwks.json` -> verification failed locally until I supplied `--kid k-20250707-rot1` and used the public key from new JWKS; then verification succeeds. So new JWKS is fine.
kevin sec: that suggests our control plane didn't pick up the new JWKS. We must ensure we reload JWKS and truststore gracefully.
marisol oncall: action items assigned:
- adele: call control-plane refresh API and watch logs
- leo: prepare truststore hot-reload and confirm commands
- kevin: coordinate risk approval for rolling reload across private control plane clusters
- marisol: coordinate with Ridgeway SRE and prepare customer update

adele eng: calling refresh API now: `POST https://private-control.redwood.internal/ridgeway/refresh-oidc` -> `202 Accepted`
adele eng: logs:
``
2025-07-07T18:18:12Z authsvc[pid=4421]: refresh requested for tenant=ridgetway id=ridgeway
2025-07-07T18:18:13Z authsvc: jwks fetch -> 200 OK
2025-07-07T18:18:13Z authsvc: parsed 2 keys, selected kid=k-20250707-rot1
2025-07-07T18:18:13Z authsvc: replacing keyset and invalidating cache for tenant=ridgeway
```
marisol oncall: good. leo, truststore?
leo infra: hot-load truststore via config agent: `POST https://config-agent.private/reload-truststore?tenant=ridgeway` returns 200.
leo infra: gateway logs show:
``
2025-07-07T18:18:40Z gateway: loaded truststore entries: Ridgeway-Int-2025
2025-07-07T18:18:41Z gateway: mTLS verify succeeded for 10/10 pending handshakes
```
marisol oncall: traffic now? Any green?
ops-bot: INC_METRIC: ridgeway.vpc.auth_errors count=1200 -> 60 (1m window)
ridgeway-sre: seeing a drop in 401s, some retries still fail but decreasing. thank you.
marisol oncall: routing note: we also activated temporary canary route to Hosted fallback for write-heavy tenants at 18:19 UTC for ~5% of traffic. will revert after confirming stability.
adele eng: verifying token verification: we decoded several incoming tokens and they now validate with new keyset. pushing a control-plane restart to clear any remaining stale caches across pods (rolling restart, 1/3 at a time): `kubectl rollout restart deployment/authsvc -n ridgeway-private` — rolling.
leo infra: restarted ingress-proxy pods and dedicated-pool ingress service. health checks green.
kevin sec: approving continuation of rolling restarts. No signs of compromise; keys rotated by Ridgeway as expected.
marisol oncall: customer comms drafted:
``
Hi Ridgeway team,
We identified your recent key & cert rotation caused a temporary mismatch with our cached JWKS and truststore, which resulted in 401s and mTLS handshakes failing for some requests. We forced a JWKS refresh and hot-reloaded the truststore; traffic is stable and we've routed a small % to Hosted fallback during the mitigation. We're monitoring for 1 hour and will confirm full recovery.
Apologies for the disruption.
```
ridgeway-sre: please add timeline and confirmation when fully recovered.
adele eng: rolling restart completed at 18:26. authsvc pod counts 3/3 ready. logs show normal token validation.
ops-bot: DEPLOY: authsvc rollout completed at 2025-07-07T18:26:40Z
marisol oncall: summary update to @pagerduty: initial detection 18:10, key rotation by customer at 18:04, errors spike 18:10-18:18, JWKS refresh + truststore reload 18:18, roll restart completed 18:26, traffic normalized 18:27.
ops-bot: INCIDENT: RIDGEWAY-VPC-AUTH - status=resolved by marisol oncall at 2025-07-07T18:33:02Z
marisol oncall: resolved for now. Follow-ups (owners):
- adele: add auto JWKS rotation detector and immediate refresh (due in sprint)
- leo: improve truststore syncing to include intermediate overlap support (create runbook)
- kevin: review customer onboarding docs for cert rotation guidance and add preflight checks for CA chain
- marisol: schedule 1:1 with Ridgeway SRE to discuss coordinated rotations and a test window
ridgeway-sre: thanks team. we'll coordinate a staged rotation next time. appreciate the fast response.
kevin sec: also add monitoring alert for `jwks_kid_mismatch` and `truststore_mismatch` so PD pages to infra+sec together.
marisol oncall: closing thread; will file postmortem doc. :white_check_mark:
